_comment: TRUST POLICY for the CI read role — GitHub Actions OIDC, no static keys.
GitHub hands the workflow a short-lived OIDC token; AWS STS exchanges it for
credentials that expire in an hour. Nothing long-lived exists to leak, to
rotate, or to find in a repository secret five years from now.
The `sub` condition is the whole security of this arrangement, so it is
pinned narrowly and NEVER written as `repo:${github_org}/*`: any workflow in
any repository of the org would otherwise be able to assume this role. It is
scoped to one repository AND one GitHub Environment, so a pull request from a
fork — which cannot reach a protected environment — gets nothing.
aud is checked as well; a token minted for a different audience is not a token
